{{pagebanner|The 9 Empirer Gods Butterworth 北海斗母宫 - panoramio (cropped).jpg}} '''Butterworth''' is the main town on the mainland side of [[Penang]] state in [[Malaysia]]. It was named after William John Butterworth, governor of the Straits Settlements from 1843-1855. [[File:BUTTERWORTH DOCKS MALAYSIA JAN 2012 (7014895773).jpg|thumb|Butterworth Docks]] Smaller, more industrial and practical, Butterworth does not have any of the atmosphere which [[George Town (Malaysia)|George Town]] across the Penang Straits has. However, it is an important transportation hub for all train and many bus services which do not go directly to Penang Island. Butterworth is also the mainland terminal for the Penang Ferry. ==Get in== ===By train=== [[File:Butterworth New 1.jpg|thumb|Butterworth Railway Station]] {{marker|type=go|name=Butterworth railway station|lat=5.3933 | long=100.3666 |image =Butterworth KTM Station, Main Entrance (to Jalan Bagan Dalam and BORR) 20230305 110831.jpg}} is next to the bus and ferry terminal, south of the town centre. It is a major rail terminal for [http://www.ktmb.com.my/ Keretapi Tanah Melayu] (Malayan Railways), with ETS trains heading south to [[Ipoh]], [[Kuala Lumpur]] and [[Johor Bahru]] and Komuter trains heading north to [[Padang Besar (Malaysia)|Padang Besar]] on the border with [[Thailand]], where connecting trains to [[Hat Yai]] and [[Bangkok]] are operated by [https://www.dticket.railway.co.th/ State Railways of Thailand]. In December 2015, electrifying and double-tracking is completed up to the Thai border. Although overnight express trains to [[Bangkok]] and [[Kuala Lumpur]] were canceled, new ETS and Komuter trains, capable of traveling up to 140 km/h, link [[Kuala Lumpur]] in just four hours and Padang Besar in less than two hours. * '''To/from [[Kuala Lumpur]] and [[Johor]]'''
There are seven ETS trains traveling to/from [[Kuala Lumpur]], with one of those originating in [[Segamat]], and one all the way from [[Johor Bahru]]. Seats on these trains are often sold out, so book in advance either at the KTMB office in the Georgetown ferry terminal, or on-line at [https://www.ktmb.com.my/ KTMB website] or other third party booking site such as [https://www.busonlineticket.com/ BusOnlineTicket.com] or [https://www.easybook.com/ Easybook.com]. * '''To/from [[Thailand]]'''
KTMB operates Komuter trains traveling to/from Padang Besar at the Thai border hourly from 05:25 to 21:25. The fair is RM11.40 and travel time is one hour and 50 minutes. From Padang Besar, [https://www.dticket.railway.co.th/ State Railways of Thailand] operates twice daily shuttle trains to [[Hat Yai]], that costs 80 [[Thailand#Money|baht]] and takes 50 minutes, and once daily express train to [[Bangkok]]. Alternatively, there are frequent local buses from the Thai side of the border to [[Hat Yai]]. Thai time is ''::one hour behind'': Malaysian time: check departure time of Thai trains are either in Thai or Malaysian time. Border formalities are done inside the Padang Besar station but there is no ATM or official currency exchange inside the station, and it is advisable to exchange some Thai baht before heading there. Refer to the [http://www.train36.com/penang-padang-besar-komuter-train.html KTMB site] for schedule. * '''To/from [[Taiping]]'''
KTMB also operates Komuter train south towards [[Taiping]]. It is also possible to make a connection there to more ETS trains to [[Kuala Lumpur]] and further south to [[Gemas]]. For schedule, refer to [http://www.train36.com/ktm-komuter-timetable.html Train36 website] ===By bus=== [[File:Penang Sentral Bus Terminal, Butterworth 20230307 104821.jpg|thumb|Penang Sentral building]] [[File:Bus platform of Penang Sentral, Butterworth 20230304 201254.jpg|thumb|Local stage-bus platform at Penang Sentral Bus Terminal]] The {{marker|type=go|name=Penang Sentral|lat=5.3944828812007986 | long=100.36552395655868| url=https://www.penangsentral.com.my/|image=Penang Sentral Bus Terminal, Butterworth 20230307 104827.jpg}} bus station is a few metres from the train station, under the highway overpass. Any train station representative can point you in the direction of the bus stop. Buses go into many destinations throughout the country. * '''To/from [[Kuala Lumpur]]''' - almost hourly, journey takes 5 hours and costs around RM25. If you are in a rush to get to KL, the bus may be your best bet. The journey time can be half as long. Most of the coaches have air-con, as well as other comforts. The buses, in most cases, do not have restrooms. However, the buses make a number of breaks at rest stops, which have restrooms, food and drinks available. Much of the journey is very scenic. :Beware of touts that looks friendly and helpful, preying on tourists at the bus station. Instead of selling tickets; they sell am overpriced voucher which you later exchange for a ticket. * [[Kuala Perlis]], RM50, three times per day. ===By road=== [[File:Butterworth, SPU District 20230701 192857.jpg|thumb|Terminal Feri Interchange of Butterworth Outer Ring Road]] City is accessible by the Butterworth Outer Ring Road and the Butterworth–Kulim Expressway, the latter is part of the North–South Expressway. ===By boat=== [[File:Sultan Abdul Halim Terminal, Butterworth 20250915 140239.jpg|thumb|Butterworth Ferry Terminal]] The much-loved Penang ferry departs regularly from the {{marker|type=go|name=Butterworth Ferry Terminal|lat=5.3948 | long=100.3636|image=Sultan Abdul Halim Terminal, Butterworth 20250915 140232.jpg}} for George Town. The ferry terminal is connected with the railway station and bus terminal via covered walkways. Direction from the train station to the ferry terminal (''terminal feri'') are well signposted. Travellers may want to consider using toilets at their hotels or at restaurants as the ferry toilets are infamous for their overuse and offensive odours. The old car ferries have been decommissioned, and the new ferries only carry pedestrians, bicycles and motorcycles. ==Get around== {{Mapframe|5.404 |100.385|height=470|zoom=12|width=470}} [http://www.rapidpg.com.my/ '''Rapid Penang'''] - bus service that covers most of the city as well as entire Penang state. ==See== [[File:temple b1.jpg|thumb|Temple of the Ninth Emperor God]] * {{see | name=Temple of the Ninth Emperor God | url=http://www.towbookong.org.my/ | email= | address=Jl Raja Uda | lat=5.4403309 | long=100.385526| directions= | phone=+60 4 331-8717 | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | content=This is a very beautiful temple with impressive architecture. The sculptures and carvings are very neat and nice. The temple was constructed in 2000 by about 50 craftsmen from China. It has three grand prayer halls, replacing an older temple that was built next to it in 1971. It's being decorated for the annual Nine Emperor Gods (Kew Ong Yeah) festival on every 9th month of Chinese Lunar Calendar. }} * {{see | name=Pantai Bersih Beach | alt=Pantai Bagan Ajam | url= | email= | address=Bagan Ajam | lat=5.443048 | long=100.3789 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Pantai Bersih, Bagan Ajam 20230628 183110.jpg | lastedit=2016-05-28 | content=Sandy beach, famous for its seafood restaurants and a popular picnic spot among locals. }} ===Outside of the city=== * {{see | name=Penang Bird Park | url=http://www.penangbirdpark.com.my/ | email=pengbird@tm.net.my | address=Jl Todak, Seberang Jaya, Perai | lat=5.3939327 | long=100.3939505 | directions= | phone=+60 4 399-1899 | tollfree= | fax= | hours=Daily 09:00-19:00 | price=RM38 for adult and RM20 for children below 12 year-old | lastedit=2016-05-28| content=This is the first and the largest bird park of its kind in Malaysia. It houses more than 300 species of birds from throughout the world, of which about half are Malaysian species. Experience hand-feeding birds in the geodesic domes and two giant-sized walk-in-aviaries. Two bird shows daily at 11:30 and 15:30. To get there take a 10-minute bus ride from Butterworth Ferry Terminal. The park receives a fair bit of negative reviews due to the bad conditions in which birds are kept, although other people find it attractive enough and worth a visit.}} * {{see | name=Air Hitam Dalam Educational Forest| alt=Hutan Pelajaran Air Hitam Dalam| url=https://www.facebook.com/airhitamdalam/ | email= | address= | lat=5.4521309 | long=100.451086| directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | lastedit=2016-05-28 | content=A protected recreation park, mostly unknown to the public.
